rows.text: “You kill men from fear. You never give them a chance to speak.”
rows.context: Melos called across the hall, “You kill men from fear. You never give them a chance to speak.”
rows.basis: Melos calls out to the ruler and criticizes him.

rows.text: “Give me three days to see my sister’s wedding,”
rows.context: “Give me three days to see my sister’s wedding,” Melos said. “Then I will return to you.”
rows.basis: Melos asks the ruler for three days to attend his sister’s wedding.

rows.context: Give me three days to see my sister’s wedding,” Melos said. “Then I will return to you.”
rows.basis: Melos promises the ruler that he will return.

rows.text: “Your friend must stay here. Return late, and he will die in your place.”
rows.context: The ruler smiled and said, “Your friend must stay here. Return late, and he will die in your place.”
rows.basis: The ruler says Melos’s friend must remain as a hostage.

rows.text: “Go now, because I know you will come back.”
rows.context: “Go now, because I know you will come back.”
rows.basis: Melos’s friend encourages him to go and expresses confidence that he will return.
Melos arrives at the square and calls out that he has returned.

rows.context: “I almost left you to die,” he said softly.
rows.basis: Melos confesses to his friend that he nearly left him to die.

rows.text: “I almost lost my trust in you,”
rows.context: “I almost lost my trust in you,” his friend replied.
rows.basis: Melos’s friend replies that he nearly lost trust in him.

rows.text: “Put the sword down and free both men.”
rows.context: Finally, he said, “Put the sword down and free both men.”
rows.basis: The ruler orders the sword lowered and both men freed.

rows.text: “How can a man win such trust?”
rows.context: More softly, he then asked, “How can a man win such trust?”
rows.basis: The ruler asks how someone can earn such trust.
